extended:
**EXCEPTIONAL QUANTUM GEOMETRY**

*AND PARTICLE PHYSICS*

37 pp, 23 sections.

**Abstract.** Based on an interpretation of the quark-lepton symmetry in terms of the unimodularity of the color group SU(3) and on the existence of 3 generations, we develop an argumentation suggesting that the “ﬁnite quantum space” corresponding to the exceptional real Jordan algebra of dimension 27 (the Euclidean Albert algebra) is relevant for the description of internal spaces in the theory of particles. In par- ticular, the triality which corresponds to the 3 oﬀ-diagonal octonionic elements of the exceptional algebra is associated to the 3 generations of the Standard Model while the representation of the octonions as a complex 4-dimensional space C ⊕C3 is associated to the quark-lepton symmetry, (one complex for the lepton and 3 for the corresponding quark).

**Outline.** Front matter; 1 Introduction; 2.1 SU(3)-spaces; 2.2 SU(3)-algebra version of octonion algebra; 2.3 The quark-lepton symmetry; 2.4 Gauge theoretical aspect; 3.1 the 3-generations; 3.2 Finite quantum spaces; 3.3 The exceptional finite quantum space; 3.4 Exceptional almost classical quantum space; 4 Modules and fundamental fermions; 4.1 Modules over Jordan algebras; 4.3 Modules for the two families by generation; 4.5 Charge conjugation; 5 Differential calculus over Jordan algebras; 5.1 First order differential calculi; 5.3 Differential graded Jordan algebras; 5.4 Higher order derivation-based differential
